checked.found: 10 April 1848 Kennington Common; march to Parliament blocked by police, petition went on by cab (History Today and Hansard accounts)
13 November 1887; about 2,000 police and 400 soldiers halted the unemployment/Irish Coercion protest march
1894; Ohio businessman Jacob Coxey, public-works jobs demand, Panic of 1893 depression
3 March 1913, day before Wilson's inauguration, Pennsylvania Avenue, heckling and hostile crowds

International Women's Day 1917 (8 March N.S.); women textile workers of the Vyborg district struck over bread shortages, protests grew into the fall of the tsar. Wikipedia's February Revolution page names Putilov strikers, but the Reading and Jacobin pieces support textile workers

1922 march organised by the National Unemployed Workers' Committee Movement; contingents converged on London from across Britain (entered London about 15 November 1922); it set the pattern for later marches (1929, 1930, 1932, 1934, 1936). The Wikipedia hunger-marches page does not detail it, but the NUWM page and search sources agree on 1922
Protests in every major city of North America and Europe and beyond in 1927, before the executions on 23 August 1927; both men Italian-born anarchists tried in Massachusetts
1932; about 17,000 WWI veterans with families, shantytown on Anacostia Flats, demanded immediate payment of service-bonus certificates
5-31 October 1936, about 200 men (185 named) from Jarrow, Tyneside, petition for work presented 4 November; shipyard closed 1934
February-March 1943 (arrests from 27 Feb, protest about seven days, men released from 6 March); non-Jewish wives outside Jewish community building at Rosenstrasse 2-4
21 February 1952: Section 144 banned gatherings in Dhaka, students gathered anyway, police fired. The wider movement spans 1948-56, but 1952 is the standard dating of the protests and the shooting
4-7 April 1958, four days, Trafalgar Square to the Atomic Weapons Research Establishment; the CND symbol was presented 21 February 1958 and used on this march
1960 protests peaking in June, hundreds of thousands around the National Diet in Tokyo against the revised US-Japan Security Treaty
1981 march of Welsh women to RAF Greenham Common, Berkshire, against US cruise missiles; camp began 5 September 1981
30 November-3 December 1999; at least 40,000 protesters, blockades prevented delegates reaching the summit, drew international attention to anti-globalisation

15 February 2003, about 800 cities, millions of participants; Guinness listed it as the largest protest in human history (the page does not use the word coordinated, but it was a single global day of action)
Began 17 September 2011 in Zuccotti Park; We are the 99% slogan; inspired wider Occupy movement abroad
28 September-15 December 2014, 79 days; umbrellas against pepper spray; main roads occupied; demand for real universal suffrage
21 January 2017, the day after Trump's inauguration; millions in the US and worldwide; pussyhats
September 2022 after Mahsa Amini died in custody, arrested for improper hijab; nationwide protests; slogan Woman, Life, Freedom
